feature: The colour picker can be driven by a scripted walk
summary: A playtest walk can now open the colour picker and use it: press the Solid, Linear, Radial and Angular tabs, switch between HSL, RGB and HEX, pick a swatch off any of the four rows, add or remove a gradient stop, save the colour as a style and close the picker. Until now a walk could open it and take a photograph of it and nothing else, so every feature inside the picker reached you as a picture.
setup: Nothing to turn on. This is a change to how the loop drives the app, so the thing to judge is the walk log, not a new control. Run it with: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/picker-controls-walk.json

try.do: Run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/picker-controls-walk.json and wait for it to say ok.
Open /tmp/photonz-playtest/picker-controls/panel-2-open.json and read the control list: the picker's own controls stand in it beside the panel's.
Read the Fill line in the log at stages 4-linear through 8-solid: it walks linear ramp of 2, linear ramp of 3, radial, angular, then back to one flat colour.
Read stage 11-shade-picked: pressing "Shades 5" put #E1A632 on the rectangle.
Read stage 13-style-saved: Save style, a typed name and the Save beside it were all pressed, and Blush is on the Library shelf.
Open the picker yourself in the dev app and check nothing about it changed. Every marker is invisible and probe-only.

evaluate: Is "Shades 5" a name you would guess for the fifth swatch on the shades row, or would you reach for the hex first?
The picker remembers which swatch row you left it on between launches, so it opened on Related rather than Shades. Is that the right thing for it to remember?
The saturation square and the four channel sliders still cannot be driven, only photographed. Is that a gap worth closing next, or is picking a swatch enough for the walks you care about?
The eyedropper is deliberately unreachable, because pressing it would raise the system screen sampler and hang the walk. Does that leave a hole in anything you wanted covered?
Does a Fill line that reads "#F6E4C1, linear ramp of 3" tell you what you need about a gradient, or do you want the stops listed?
rough: The Screen Recording grant was on, so both pictures here are real screen captures of the probe, not offscreen renders.

A swatch is named by its place in the row, not by its colour, because the shades are worked out from whatever colour the picker opened on: a walk that said #7C4DFF would break the first time the colour before it changed. The hex is in the detail, so the log still says which colour landed.
Because the swatch row is sticky across launches, a walk that wants the shades has to press Shades first rather than assuming. That is a real trap and it cost this walk one failed run.
The gradient aim pad and the ramp itself are still out of reach for the same reason as the sliders: aiming is a drag, not a press.
